title: Polished minimal SDK starter pack: Next.js frontend, FastAPI microservice, Go HTTP worker, CLI cookbook
creator: Maya Chen
description: Deliver a compact, production-oriented starter pack that demonstrates best-practice patterns across Redwood SDKs (TypeScript, Python, Go) focused on: ergonomic streaming, robust retry/backoff policies, cancellation patterns, and small cookbook snippets for common app archetypes (Next.js, FastAPI microservice, Go HTTP worker, and a CLI utility). Goal: make a 15–30 minute onboarding path for engineers that proves reliable defaults and shows how to tune for latency/cost.
acceptance_criteria: Four runnable example repos (Next.js, FastAPI, Go HTTP, CLI) with minimal configuration and clear README
Each example shows SDK usage for: auth, retry/backoff, streaming (client & server side), graceful cancellation, and sane defaults for batch/cache where applicable
Automated smoke test workflow that spins up local examples and validates generation + streaming end-to-end
Design/Docs sign-off from Developer Experience and SDK owners
A merged PR that publishes templates under github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-examples/minimal-pack and a console quickstart page linking each template
steps: Define API surface for examples: TS (nextjs + client lib), Python (FastAPI server & client), Go (http worker and client helper), CLI (node-based, using SDK) - 1 day

Implement streaming helper abstractions: TypeScript async-iterable wrapper with AbortSignal integration; Python async generator + contextmanager; Go channel-based streamer with context cancel - 2 days
Standardize retry policy and config: exponential backoff with jitter, idempotency guidance for non-repeatable calls, built-in telemetry hooks - 1 day

Wire templates: build minimal Next.js app that streams chat responses, FastAPI endpoint that proxies Redwood calls with request tracing, Go worker showing queued streaming and KV cache hints, simple CLI for prompt experiments - 3 days
Add CI smoke tests and GitHub Actions to validate examples and run linters/formatters - 1 day
Internal review + iterate on ergonomics from SDK owners and DX - 2 days
Publish templates, update docs site quickstart, and create a short demo video for onboarding - 1 day

technical_notes: TypeScript: recommend createStreamingIterable(response) -> AsyncIterable<string|TokenDelta> that accepts AbortSignal for cancellation and exposes a .close() helper
Python: streaming with 'async for token in client.stream()' inside 'async with client.streaming_session() as s:' to scope KV cache hints and telemetry
Go: use context.Context for cancellation; streamer returns (chan Token, chan error) pattern and a Close(ctx) to flush cache/prefetch
Retries: default 3 attempts for transient network errors, exponential backoff base 200ms, max 5s, full jitter; idempotency guidance for non-repeatable operations (e.g., create-only calls)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: examples become stale as SDK surface changes. Mitigation: add CI job that runs example smoke tests on SDK integration branches and bump examples in SDK release checklist.

Risk: streaming ergonomics differ between runtimes leading to inconsistent DX. Mitigation: converge on the same conceptual primitives (abort/cancel + async-iterable/async-generator + token deltas) and document mapping between languages.
Risk: customers copy templates with insecure defaults. Mitigation: include explicit security section in each README and make production notes (KMS, env var handling, no hardcoded keys).
